transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because there’s been some trouble in my husband’s family, and I don’t want to sound like I’m making a big thing out of nothing. But his sister has been working things with the family business, and I really believe she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to tell me it’s fine or smooth it over, but I’ve been seeing it for more than a year now.
Do you think others are aware of your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions?

I think some of them are aware, yes… or at least they’ve noticed things. They just try to smooth it over and tell me not to worry, like I’m reading too much into it. I don’t want to cause trouble, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year—she’s working the family business so she can get control of the money and leave me out of decisions.
Do you think your husband's sister is actually trying to harm you or your relationship with your husband, or is it just about the business decisions?

I don’t want to say she’s trying to hurt me, exactly… I know that sounds strong. It feels more like she’s been working the family business so she can get control of the money, and then I’m left out of decisions. People keep telling me to let it go or that it’s not that serious, but I’ve been seeing it for over a year now.
Do you think your interpretation of your husband's sister's actions is something that might be misunderstood by others or is it something you're absolutely certain about?

I mean… I know other people might say I’m misunderstanding it, and I don’t want to sound stubborn or like I’m accusing someone unfairly. But to me, I’m pretty certain. I came in because my husband’s sister has been working things with the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. Folks keep trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your husband's sister might not be trying to push you out of decisions?

I’ve tried to consider it, yes… I don’t want to be unfair to her or make something out of nothing. But I keep coming back to what I’ve seen. She’s been working things with the family business so she can get control of the money, and it leaves me pushed out of decisions. People try to smooth it over, and I understand why, but this has been going on for more than a year now.
Do you think it's possible that you could be wrong about your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions?

I guess anything is possible, and I don’t want to sound like I’m being unreasonable. But… I came here because I really do believe my husband’s sister has been working the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, and maybe they mean well, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister is something that you might change your mind about if you found out more information?

I mean… if there was real information, I’d try to listen. I don’t want to be the kind of person who just digs in and won’t hear anything else, you know? But from what I’ve seen, I don’t think it would change much. I came because his sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, and maybe they’re trying to help, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think there's any chance at all that your husband's sister is not trying to push you out of decisions?

I suppose there’s always some chance, and I don’t want to sound stubborn or like I’m blaming her just to blame her. But honestly… I came because I really believe my husband’s sister has been working things with the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. Folks keep trying to smooth it over, and I know they may mean well, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions could be considered a certainty that you hold, even if others disagree?

Yes… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m being difficult or like I won’t listen to anybody. But it does feel like a certainty to me, yes. I came here because my husband’s sister has been working the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and no matter how people try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister could be false?

I mean… I guess anything could be false in theory, right? I don’t want to sound like I think I know everything. But no, I don’t really believe this is false. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and even if folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think there's anything that could change your mind about your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions?

I mean… I’d like to say yes, because I don’t want to seem unreasonable. If there was something real clear, I’d try to listen, doctor. But honestly, I don’t know what would change my mind at this point. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister is something that you cannot change, no matter what happens?

I don’t want to say “no matter what” like I’m stubborn, doctor. I’d like you to think I’m trying to be fair. But… yes, it feels pretty fixed for me. I came because my husband’s sister has been working the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and people can smooth it over all they want, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Is your belief about your husband's sister affecting your daily activities or relationships?

A little, I suppose… not terribly, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function. I still do my regular things around the house, and I still go to church and all that.

But I have skipped some family get-togethers, just to avoid the tension. And I do keep certain plans or money matters more to myself now, because I don’t want them getting back to my husband’s sister. I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed any change in your relationship with your husband due to your concerns about his sister?

Some, yes… but I don’t want you to think we’re falling apart or anything. We still talk, and I still do my usual routines, go to church, take care of things.

It’s more that I’ve skipped some family get-togethers, because I just don’t want the tension around his sister. And I do keep certain plans or money matters more to myself now, so they don’t get back to her. I know that probably doesn’t sound ideal, but I’m just trying to protect myself, if that makes sense.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister is based on facts or is it more of a feeling you have?

I’d like to think it’s based on facts, doctor. I know people may say it’s just my feeling, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but I’ve been watching how my husband’s sister is in the family business and how she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out of decisions.

Maybe I don’t have some official proof in my hand, but no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister could be considered a delusion by others?

I suppose other people might call it that, if they don’t see what I see. I’m not trying to sound unreasonable, Doctor, really.

But I came here because my husband’s sister has been working things in the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister could change if you were presented with evidence that contradicts it?

I mean… I’d try to listen, Doctor. I don’t want to seem like I’m just refusing anything anyone says. If there was real evidence, I’d look at it.

But it would have to really explain what I’ve been seeing, because I came here because his sister has been working things in the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, but this has been going on for more than a year, and I know what I’ve seen.
Has your belief about your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions changed at all since you first started noticing it?

Not really, no… I mean, I’ve tried to be fair about it, and I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But since I first started noticing it, it’s mostly just gotten clearer to me.

I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, and I understand maybe they don’t want trouble in the family, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
Do you think there is any possibility, no matter how small, that you could be completely wrong about your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions?

I mean… I guess I’m supposed to say there’s always some tiny possibility, right? I don’t want to seem stubborn or like I won’t listen.

But, Doctor, honestly… I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. So… completely wrong? That’s hard for me to believe.
Do you think you will ever be able to change your mind about your husband's sister trying to push you out of decisions?

I’d like to think I could, if someone showed me something that truly made sense of it. I don’t want to be unreasonable, Doctor.

But right now… I don’t really see how. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, and maybe they mean well, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. So changing my mind would be… hard.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, fixed belief that her husband's sister is trying to push her out of decisions regarding the family business, despite others' attempts to reassure her. This belief has been held for over a year and is not altered by contrary evidence or reassurance, meeting the criteria for a delusional disorder.
